target_customer: Mid size and large enterprises, including financial services and healthcare, whose security, IT and finance teams need to see and control employee use of AI tools.
problem: Companies use dozens of unapproved AI tools and agents, leaking data and spending unmanaged money, and cannot see or govern that usage.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS with on device agents or network deployment, priced per device or deployment (pricing not found)
product_category: AI governance, shadow AI discovery and AI security

founders.name: Naman Ambavi
founders.background_notes: Listed as sole founder on YC page; a profile site says he founded solo in 2025 and is 23, which is not a primary source so age is not recorded.

competitors.name: WitnessAI
competitors.what: Enterprise AI governance and security platform

competitors.name: Harmonic Security
competitors.what: Prompt level inspection of AI usage across tools

competitors.name: Prompt Security
competitors.what: Generative AI security, acquired by SentinelOne in August 2025
competitors.traction_then: Acquired at a reported 250 to 300 million valuation

competitors.name: Nightfall AI
competitors.what: SaaS and endpoint data loss prevention extended to AI

technical_complexity.rationale: Network and device level inspection of AI traffic plus an on device model and a policy engine is substantial but uses known patterns; keeping detection current as AI tools change is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded rivals and acquirers in the same wedge; some stickiness from deployed agents and policy configuration.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Security platforms were already buying or building the same wedge, for example SentinelOne acquiring Prompt Security in August 2025.

market_need_then: Enterprise shadow AI was a widely discussed problem; the YC launch post cites a financial firm that found 63 AI tools against 15 approved, a company claim.

identity.voice_and_tone: Command and control framing: 'Take command of the AI your company already runs on'; earlier launch note line 'You can't govern what you can't see'.

branding.brand_signature: Oxi-1, its on device model name

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline but no press about the brand itself, no community, and name similar to oxygen product names; evidence limited to its own site and profile pages.

outcome_analysis: Oximy is a Winter 2026 YC company building AI governance and shadow AI controls for enterprises, with a solo founder, a team of 8, a named advisor group of former CISOs and CIOs, and a list of investors on its site including Peak XV, Blume, Schema Ventures and Seven Stars. It is too early to judge an outcome. The main risk is a crowded category where large security vendors are buying competitors, and traction claims such as 50,000 monitored devices are company reported.
notes: Aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, Neuronfeed) report about 500 thousand dollars as a convertible note or pre seed in early 2026, with YC and angel Sudarshan Sridharan; seen only in aggregators so not recorded as a round. Oximy's own site lists Peak XV, Blume, Schema, Seven Stars, SF1, Timeless as investors but no round amounts or dates; a search for a Peak XV led seed announcement found none. Competitor sources are 2025 and 2026 comparison pages by vendors and are marketing; dated close to the batch only loosely. Company claims (50,000 devices, 6,000 tools, SOC 2 Type I) are unverified and differ across pages (3,500 versus 5,000 versus 6,000 tools). No source gives the name origin. Outcome search covered competitor acquisitions only; none about Oximy found.
